definition: The fraction of actual positives correctly identified — sensitivity or recall, trading off against false positives.
details: The fraction of actual positives correctly identified — sensitivity or recall, trading off against false positives.

explainer.lead: The true positive rate is the fraction of actual positives that a model correctly identifies, also called sensitivity or recall. It matters because it trades off directly against false positives.

tiers.eli5: Of all the things that really are 'yes', how many did the model correctly catch.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to measure detection coverage and to set thresholds; a common pitfall is pushing the rate up and accepting many false positives in return.
tiers.paperLevel: True positive rate is the fraction of actual positives correctly identified, i.e. sensitivity or recall, trading off against false positives.

explainer.example: If 80 of 100 actual positives are detected, the true positive rate is 0.8.
